# Critical cap BM equality: equal sections and a four-facet obstruction

The first-variation mechanism and support equations below were proposed
independently by root and checked here. This note proves their precise
scope. It does not assert a general gluing theorem for all critical cap
covers or for arbitrary numbers of mixed-integer fibers.

## 1. Genuine middle criticality forces equality of the endpoint sections

Let d>=2 and let an actual source have precisely three positive
d-dimensional convex fibers A,K,B at integer bases -1,0,1. Let y in K,
and write a closed through-(0,y) ambient halfspace as

    H_alpha={ (z,x):u.x+alpha z>=u.y },

where u!=0. Suppose both endpoint cuts are proper: their boundary
hyperplanes meet the interiors of A and B, so the cuts and their
strict complements have positive d-volume. Assume H_alpha attains
the raw halfspace depth at this fixed point (0,y). A globally critical
cap at a deepest point is a special case of this hypothesis.

For D=A or B, let

    F_D(t)=|D intersect {u.x>=t}|,
    sigma_D(t)=H_(d-1)(D intersect {u.x=t}).

At a proper level, the section area is positive and continuous. For
d>=2, this follows from Brunn--Minkowski concavity of its
1/(d-1)-power on the interior projection interval. Concavity there
implies continuity. Integrating the sections gives

    F_D'(t)=-sigma_D(t)/|u|.

Changing only alpha keeps (0,y) on the cap plane and keeps the middle
contribution fixed. The cap mass as a function of alpha is exactly

    F_A(u.y+alpha)+|K intersect {u.x>=u.y}|+F_B(u.y-alpha).

Both endpoint levels remain proper for sufficiently small changes.
Its derivative vanishes at a minimizing alpha, so

    sigma_A(u.y+alpha)=sigma_B(u.y-alpha).             (1)

No differentiability at a supporting endpoint is used, and no derivative
of a sampled fiber-volume sum is replaced by a continuous-base integral.

## 2. Captured-side BM equality now makes the endpoint caps translates

Suppose also that this SAME actual cap has exact captured-side BM:

    |K intersect H_0|^(1/d)
      =(|A intersect H_-1|^(1/d)+|B intersect H_1|^(1/d))/2.

The actual midpoint inclusion of the two endpoint caps lies in K's
cap, because their two thresholds average to u.y. Equality in the
ordinary positive-volume BM inequality therefore forces a positive
homothety

    B intersect H_1=lambda(A intersect H_-1)+v,
    lambda>0.

The artificial cut facet is the minimizing u-face of each cap. The
homothety must map this face to its counterpart. Consequently

    sigma_B(u.y-alpha)=lambda^(d-1)sigma_A(u.y+alpha).

The section measure in (1) is positive. Since d>=2, (1) implies
lambda=1. Thus the two endpoint caps are actual translates and have
equal volume. The numerical equality gives the same volume for the
middle cap as well. In particular, if their total raw mass is Q,
each of the three captured contributions equals Q/3.

The restriction d>=2 is essential: in dimension one the cut section
has counting measure one independently of the positive homothety
ratio, so the exponent d-1 supplies no such conclusion.

Equal endpoint CAP volumes do not assert equal whole-body volumes.
Unequal homothetic simplices, cut at suitably adjusted levels, can
have congruent endpoint caps. No global homothety is inferred yet.

## 3. The fixed four-facet family and its cap combinatorics

For a support vector a=(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4), write

    P(a)={ (x,y):
        -3x+y<=a_1, -x-2y<=a_2,
        x<=a_3, x+y<=a_4 }.

Assume all four facets are active, with positive edge lengths, in this
cyclic order. The vertices are p_12,p_23,p_34,p_41, obtained by
intersecting the corresponding successive facet lines.

Let A=P(a) and B=P(b). The middle body can be any actual compatible
K for the conclusions about A,B below. Suppose there are two genuine
middle critical caps, each having proper endpoint cuts and exact
captured-side BM, with these specified combinatorics in BOTH endpoints:

* The continuous normal of the first cap is (1,0). Its cut captures
  exactly the two vertices p_23,p_34 strictly and meets the other
  adjacent edges in their interiors. Thus its cap contains the full
  original right edge, whose outer normal is (1,0).
* The continuous normal of the second cap is (-1,-1). Its cut captures
  exactly p_12,p_23 strictly, meeting the adjacent edges in their
  interiors. Thus its cap contains the full original second edge,
  whose outer normal is (-1,-2).

The integer coefficients of these two ambient caps are arbitrary and
independent. They can shift the two endpoint thresholds oppositely;
the proof does not fix those coefficients to zero.

By Section 2, each pair of corresponding endpoint caps is related by
a translation. Translation preserves each oriented edge normal and
its length. For the first cap this matches the full original right
edges; its artificial cut edge has the opposite normal and cannot
be substituted for that original edge. For the second cap it matches
the original (-1,-2) edges. The following support calculation therefore
applies regardless of those allowed threshold shifts.

## 4. The two exact edge constraints leave only global translations

The length of the right vertical edge of P(a) is

    (a_4-a_3)-[-(a_2+a_3)/2]
       =(a_2+2a_4-a_3)/2.

The second edge is parallel to (2,-1). Its endpoint x-coordinates are

    x(p_12)=-(2a_1+a_2)/7, x(p_23)=a_3.

Its length is therefore a fixed positive geometric factor times

    a_3+(2a_1+a_2)/7.

Put delta_j=b_j-a_j. Equality of the two edge lengths gives exactly

    delta_2+2delta_4-delta_3=0,
    2delta_1+delta_2+7delta_3=0.                       (2)

Define v_x=delta_3 and v_y=delta_4-delta_3. Solving (2) gives

    delta=(-3v_x+v_y, -v_x-2v_y, v_x, v_x+v_y).       (3)

These are precisely the changes of the four support numbers under
translation by v=(v_x,v_y). Hence

    B=A+v.                                           (4)

Conversely every translation gives support changes (3) and satisfies
both equations, so the kernel has been identified exactly, not just
bounded by a dimension count.

Consequently the nongluing quadrilateral cannot be upgraded to a
genuinely critical captured-side equality example while keeping this
normal fan and these two cap combinatorics. If K=(A+B)/2, then K=A+v/2
as well. This conclusion does not exclude other cap combinatorics or
different normal fans, nor does it exclude general critical cap covers.

## 5. Direct first-variation certificate for the original quadrilateral

For the explicit polygons in
`candidate 60dfb1dd651b7ddd`,
the supports are

    a=(5,4,2,1), b=(7,7/2,3/2,1/2),
    delta=(2,-1/2,-1/2,-1/2).

The first expression in (2) equals -1, while the second equals zero.
Thus those bodies violate the necessary criticality constraints.
More directly, their endpoint sections at the zero integer tilt have

    H_1: sigma_A=3, sigma_B=9/4,
    H_2: sigma_A=8/3, sigma_B=17/6,
    H_3: sigma_A=sigma_B=(13/4)sqrt(2).

The derivative of the total mixed cap mass with respect to its own
integer coefficient is consequently

    H_1: -3/4, H_2: 1/6, H_3: 0.

The first two nonzero derivatives give explicit improving cap
perturbations at the fixed middle point. This verifies directly why
the exact noncritical cap-equality counterexample cannot be treated
as a critical-cover obstruction.

## 6. Full first variation fixes the middle section centroid

Retain the hypotheses of Sections 1--2. Write E_z for the proper
endpoint or middle section on the original ambient cap boundary,
sigma_z for its (d-1)-area, and c_z for its ordinary section centroid.
The middle section is proper as well: proper endpoint cuts provide
midpoint points strictly on both sides of its plane inside K.

The exact cap-set equality and the translate conclusion show

    E_0=(E_-1+E_1)/2,
    sigma_-1=sigma_0=sigma_1=sigma>0,
    c_0=(c_-1+c_1)/2.                                (5)

Here E_-1 and E_1 lie in parallel affine planes. The equality of the
minimum-u faces follows directly from equality of the cap sets. If the
endpoint cap translation is v, the source cap is the first cap plus
v/2, so the same statements hold for their faces and centroids.

Vary the continuous normal u to u+tau v, keeping the integer
coefficient alpha fixed and writing the through-source inequality as

    (u+tau v).(x-y)+alpha z>=0.

For any v perpendicular to u, the derivative of the mixed cap mass is

    (1/|u|) sum_{z=-1}^1
          integral_{E_z} v.(x-y) dH_(d-1)(x)
      =(sigma/|u|) v.(c_-1+c_0+c_1-3y)
      =(3sigma/|u|) v.(c_0-y).                       (6)

For completeness, the derivative formula needs no smooth body
boundary. Use coordinates x-y=xi+s u/|u|, with xi perpendicular to u.
At base z the original threshold is s_z=-alpha z/|u| and the varied
threshold is s_z-tau v.xi/|u|. A vertical slice of a convex body is an
interval. For almost every xi in the proper section's relative
interior, s_z is strictly between the interval endpoints and the
slice-length derivative is v.xi/|u|. Outside the section it is zero
except on the section boundary, which has zero (d-1)-measure. The
difference quotient is bounded by |v.xi|/|u| on a fixed bounded
projection. Dominated convergence proves (6). A relative interior
point of a proper convex section belongs to the body's interior,
which justifies the strict interval assertion.

Criticality at the fixed source makes (6) zero for every v perpendicular
to u. Both c_0 and y lie in the middle cut plane, so c_0-y is already
perpendicular to u. Consequently

    c_0=y, and c_-1+c_1=2y.                          (7)

Thus every proper exact-BM critical cap has its middle cut section
centered at the source point. This says neither that y is the centroid
of K nor that the two endpoint section centroids are independent of
the cap direction. In particular the endpoint cap translations may
still vary among different critical caps.

## 7. A scoped second-variation test for a common section germ

Here is a further local consequence, with its regularity hypotheses
stated explicitly. Suppose the three fibers are polytopes, the original
cut plane contains no vertex of any fiber, and Sections 1--2 apply.
Translate the continuous coordinates by y and apply the permitted
fiber shear x -> x-z(c_1-y). This maps integer fibers to themselves
and has determinant one on each fiber. By (5)--(7), the three captured
caps and the three cutting sections now coincide, their plane is
s=0, and the original integer coefficient is zero. Rotate continuous
coordinates so their unit normal is the final coordinate vector;
write x=(xi,s).

In these coordinates the three polytopes also coincide in a sufficiently
small neighborhood of their common section. To see this, present them
by their finitely many facet inequalities. Every facet meeting the
section continues into the captured cap: the cut contains no vertex,
so no facet can have its maximum height exactly zero. Its supporting
plane is therefore fixed by the common cap. Every remaining facet
inequality has strictly positive slack on the compact section, unless
it is already a common active facet. Taking the minimum of those
finitely many positive slacks gives a common neighborhood. In particular
there is a slab thickness rho>0 in which all three bodies coincide
where the common section and its nearby sections occur.

For the middle polytope D, set

    F(v,t)=|D intersect {s+v.xi>=t}|,

for sufficiently small v in R^(d-1) and t in R. The absence of a vertex
on the original cut keeps the cut combinatorics fixed near (0,0).
Triangulation, or the explicit intersection of a moving plane with
fixed edges followed by the determinant volume formula, shows that
F is twice continuously differentiable there.

For all sufficiently small v and beta, the actual three-fiber cap mass
with inequality s+v.xi+beta z>=0 equals exactly

    G(v,beta)=F(v,beta)+F(v,0)+F(v,-beta).            (8)

Indeed the captured bodies coincide above the original plane, and the
changing threshold differs from it only in the common section
neighborhood. The three threshold changes are beta,0,-beta.
At (0,0) all cross derivatives between v and beta cancel, giving

    Hess G = diag(3 Hess_v F, 2 F_tt).               (9)

Since G has a local minimum, both blocks are positive semidefinite.
Let sigma(s) be the middle section area at height s. F_t(0,t)=-sigma(t),
so the scalar necessary condition is

    sigma'(0)<=0.                                  (10)

The other block is precisely the ordinary directional cap Hessian
of the middle body about y. Thus local criticality additionally
requires that ordinary directional Hessian to be positive semidefinite.
No sufficient global depth criterion is asserted: (9)--(10) do not
compare distant cap normals, cap combinatoric transitions, or finite
integer-tilt changes. The new trapezoid candidates may satisfy these
local conditions and still require a separate global certificate.
